 This weekend's active military conflict defied speculation about US-Iran talks following stand-offs by both parties, lifting oil prices to the highest since Jun 2025.
 


 The open confrontation increased concerns over global oil supply, with no traffic on the strait as tanker operators paused operations.
 


 The Strait of Hormuz accounts for about 20% of global oil flows, making the route one of the most essential ones.
 


 Eight OPEC+ members planned to increase output by about 206k barrels per day from Apr, gradually unwinding prior cuts to balance price strength while maintaining market share.
 


 Geopolitical headlines and this week's US economic releases may affect oil price volatility in the near future.
